paragraphs: Friend, this psalm is a long, honest look in the mirror, and it starts and ends with praise. The writer says, "We have sinned like our fathers," and he doesn't blame the oven, the dough or anybody else (Psalm 106:6). He knows the whole story of Israel forgetting, grumbling and chasing other gods, and he still opens with "Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good" (Psalm 106:1). Telling the truth about ourselves and praising God are meant to go together.

Here's the part I want you to carry out of my bakery. Over and over, God's people sank down, and over and over God stepped in. Even at the Red Sea, where they rebelled, "Yet He saved them for the sake of His name, to make His power known" (Psalm 106:7-8). Later, when they were in distress, "He heard their cry," and "He remembered His covenant with them, and relented by the abundance of His loving devotion" (Psalm 106:44-45). Their rescue never rested on how well they did, it rested on who HE is.

So what do you do with that, baker? You get honest, and you get hopeful. You can name your sin without hiding it, because His loving devotion "endures forever" (Psalm 106:1). Then you do what the writer does and turn your history into a prayer: "Save us, O LORD our God," so that we may give thanks to His holy name (Psalm 106:47). And then you say a big "Hallelujah!" with me, mustache and all (Psalm 106:48).
